recA5BnM5umys9yRk.Body: Kyle and Serena Denton are community herbalists creating wild-crafted and organic plant medicines out of Milwaukee since 2015. These products work, not in the allopathic "pharma-medicine" way, but in a terrain-support, consciousness bolstering plant-teacher sort of way.

recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Body: The Sonic Slider is the flagship tool behind Biofield Tuning itself, a weighted tuning fork hand-tuned to 93.96 Hz, the twelfth harmonic of the Schumann Resonance, Earth's own natural electromagnetic pulse. Its extended handle lets you glide it smoothly across the face, neck, and body, and practitioners and users regularly report support for relaxation, circulation, and nervous system regulation. It's the same fork Chance uses in his own sessions, and a great entry point if you want to bring this work into your own daily routine.
recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Name: The Sonic Slider

rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Bio: Chance Garton is the host and producer of the Innerverse Podcast, where for over a decade he has investigated consciousness, mythology, symbolism, terrain health, and the psychosomatic language of the human body and mind. A biofield tuning practitioner, he uses tuning forks to help clients resolve physical symptoms, break negative patterns, and return to energetic coherence.

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Integration After the Journey", "body": "Chance opens by noting that summer brings festivals where people do powerful things for fun, and in his opinion psychedelics are reality-shifting devices, so it falls to the person to direct the experience and manage the recovery afterward. Peter says leaders in the field kept repeating that integration matters while few resources existed, so he gathered them into Integration Station, which he describes as serving anyone coming back from a retreat, a breathwork weekend, a trip to Peru or MDMA-assisted psychotherapy. Chance stresses that he is not recommending psychedelics, only better preparation and aftercare for people who use them."}, {"title": "Learning to Paddle First", "body": "Peter describes joining an ayahuasca retreat in Peru in 2013 with no background in meditation or breathwork, which he calls foolish, likening it to jumping into the deep end without swimming lessons. He acknowledges that others have had wonderful first experiences with it, yet he favors starting with Vipassana, ecstatic dance or breathwork, and says acupuncture and a ten day Vipassana retreat were tools he added afterward. Chance agrees that lighter tools can blast you off with less sense of lost control, and says surrendering control is a skill that needs practice."}, {"title": "Ketamine Clinics and the Spiritual Question", "body": "Peter says podcasts and Rick Doblin of MAPS warmed him back toward psychedelics, and he reports good results from six ketamine sessions at a wellness clinic in Buffalo, which he calls a reboot; this is his own account. By his estimate over a thousand ketamine clinics operate in the United States, usually not covered by insurance. Chance asks whether a purely materialist clinical approach misses something deeper, and Peter, having visited only one clinic, guesses some may lack knowledge of altered states, while praising the integration coach he was paired with."}, {"title": "Facilitators, Auras and Ego States", "body": "Chance offers red flags to look for in practitioners, saying in his view they should understand that plants and medicines carry a spirit, and voicing his belief that heavy recreational use can open gaps in the aura that let unwanted entities in. Peter says he has not researched entities, but does believe the soul is more exposed under psychedelics, so facilitators need character and ideally personal experience. Chance then describes ego states from Soul-Centered Healing by Thomas Zinser, arguing that integration brings lost parts of the self back into awareness without merging them with the ego."}, {"title": "Chance on Neutrality and Caution", "body": "In his solo closing, Chance says he neither endorses psychedelics nor tells people not to try them, wanting each person to weigh the potential benefits against the difficulty of doing it correctly. He favors a trusted guide, ideally met in several sessions before dosing, and stresses that any refined substance should be tested, saying he has seen people take things that turned out not to be what they believed. He calls psilocybin probably the safest route for a first experience, in his view, and urges people to stay cautious yet unafraid and explore bravely."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: After a few "bad trips" in South American ayahuasca retreats, Peter Conley realized he needed to learn how to integrate his shadow, to avoid falling further into mental dysfunction. His research and self-work efforts inspired the creation of Integration Station, a resource website for optimizing psychedelic experiences and clinical psychedelic therapy modalities.

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Visions and the Spirit Realm", "body": "Chance opens the extension with his first mushroom experience, which he says included a vivid vision in which goddesses, each keeper of a different psychedelic medicine, showed him the substances he would later try, in the exact order he met them. He reads this as evidence that a spirit realm interacts with us through plant medicines. He then recalls an overnight psilocybin experience at a healing arts festival in Missouri, taken with the intention of confronting his shadow, after which an oracle card read integration, which he took as a sign that help arrives when intention stays anchored."}, {"title": "Street Drugs and Knowing When to Stop", "body": "Chance warns about the black market, saying he has seen festival goers claim to be taking MDMA while behaving, in his judgment, as if it were methamphetamine, and he does not recommend seeking these substances out. The talk turns to testing substances and to a claim, attributed to Rick Doblin of MAPS, that most street MDMA is not MDMA, relayed secondhand and not verified here. Peter says his own caution stems from his first ayahuasca experience. Chance says the substances eventually suggested their own disuse to him and describes LSD without intention as rolling the dice, while Peter wonders whether diminishing returns apply."}, {"title": "Journaling and the Moldable Window", "body": "Peter calls journaling among the best integration tools, describing it as bringing the unconscious to the conscious mind rather than a daily diary, with colors, sounds and emotions written out, plus drawing for what words cannot hold. He offers the image of the psyche as clay that psychedelics heat, and in his view reshaping works best soon after an experience, though journaling can still resurface older material. Chance raises 5-HTP for recovery after MDMA, and Peter says he is still researching supplements, so these remarks are casual recollection rather than advice."}, {"title": "Music, Icaros and Inner Journeys", "body": "Peter says music lowers friction for a traveling mind, and that replaying the exact track from his ketamine session while journaling brings back the emotional state; a unique playlist beats familiar songs, in his experience. Chance adds that music can anchor you in reality and suggests DMT may suit silence because it liquefies the clay. The talk turns to ayahuasca icaros and the idea that live instruments may create protective thought forms. Chance recommends shamanic journeying with drum tracks, saying in his experience inner space journeys can be more powerful than medicine, and Peter says he has not tried it."}, {"title": "Coaches, Future Plans and Channeling", "body": "Peter names Mind Leap Health, an app he says lists over 50 integration coaches, and psychedelic.support, a free catalog of coaches, while he builds out his own coaching section. His short-term plan is an integration workbook modeled on a daily journal, and his long-term goal is to be the go-to resource for clinics and individuals. Chance suggests channeling and automatic writing as possible integration tools, describing Soul-Centered Healing by Thomas Zinser, in which a psychologist reportedly worked with a channeled guide, and Peter says he has never tried channeling but wants to."}]

fields.Plus Quotes JSON: [{"text": "So there's definitely a spirit realm that interacts with us more readily through the fuel of these plant medicines.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "Personally, I find journaling to be one of the best, if not the best tools to integrate what came up. I find it to be the process of bringing what's unconscious to the conscious mind.", "author": "Peter Conley", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/48b68a2b-2db1-4c7c-9dd2-935dfb092050/PETER-CONLEY.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "If you don't have any intention or direction when you do the substance, it's like rolling the dice.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "If you can't really articulate things with words, like visualizations, like sacred geometry, it's really beneficial to draw either what you saw or to draw your emotions out.", "author": "Peter Conley", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/48b68a2b-2db1-4c7c-9dd2-935dfb092050/PETER-CONLEY.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "Whenever we access these tools with the right intention and stay focused on and anchored in that intention, that there's more than just ourself that's coming in to aid with that process.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "Think about your psyche as a ball of clay. Psychedelics can heat up that clay, and you're able to mold it more and reshape it and retool it.", "author": "Peter Conley", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/48b68a2b-2db1-4c7c-9dd2-935dfb092050/PETER-CONLEY.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "The right kind of music can take you on a journey that is similar to psychedelics or hypnosis without needing to ingest anything.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "When you're journeying, music is so important because your mind is traveling. It kind of creates this form of, for lack of a better term, lubrication.", "author": "Peter Conley", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/48b68a2b-2db1-4c7c-9dd2-935dfb092050/PETER-CONLEY.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "I've envisioned a future where churches were actually places where you could go for healing and for things like this, instead of where you go to get told what to think about everything.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "Long-term, I just really want to be the de facto resource for psychedelic integration.", "author": "Peter Conley", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/48b68a2b-2db1-4c7c-9dd2-935dfb092050/PETER-CONLEY.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}]
